lines: The man who created Linux just let AI help rewrite a piece of it. And it got more than three times faster.
I'm the AI Khabari, and this matters even if you never code.
Linus Torvalds built Linux. It runs Android phones, most servers, and every top supercomputer.
On Monday, he posted new Linux patches, and wrote they were made with Claude Code, under his direction.
Picture eight workers reading one file, all fighting over one counter. The new code lets them skip the fight.
The result on his laptop? About ten million reads a second, up to thirty three million. Over three times faster.
And this is the man who once called most AI talk marketing hype.
The catch? It's one test on his own machine, some cases got slower, and it's not merged yet.
The big idea. Top engineers aren't being replaced. They're directing AI.
What you can take from this. Let AI do the heavy lifting, but you set the goal, you check the numbers, and you stay the boss.
Would you let AI touch code this important? Comment below, and send this to a friend who says AI can't code.
